description: Team Blue Sphere - Alpha: two Python developers from Metro Atlanta building a fire safety dashboard from NASA microgravity combustion data. I’m an AI startup tech-founder and my team mate is a Sr. AI Engineer. We scope tightly, ship a working demo, and trace every insight to its source. Looking for:  someone with combustion or aerospace knowledge to check our science, and a storyteller for the demo video. No NASA data experience needed, just reliability and curiosity.
summary:
FlameLens is a web-based research dashboard that turns NASA’s microgravity combustion data into source-linked fire-safety insights. We built a curated library of 13 NASA PSI combustion investigations, with source excerpts and deeper condition and finding records for priority studies. 
Researchers can explore studies by prevention, detection, or suppression, compare investigations side by side (such as BASS versus BASS-II, and SAME versus FLEX), and see where the evidence has gaps. An optional AI assistant answers questions using only cited NASA excerpts. We also include a native sample of CFI-G run data from PSI and cited Earth applications, such as fine-water-mist extinguishers.

This addresses the challenge by helping users find, compare, and interpret scattered experiments, and by organizing data that supports predictive modeling. It matters because future Moon and Mars habitats may have higher oxygen levels that increase flammability. Engineers need traceable evidence, and FlameLens shows both what the research supports and what it does not.
